## INIT2 · INIT2-confined-cores — R34's core rule refuses every confined manifest on one hart

Status: **resolved** · Assigned to: Architect · Revision: 9

Evidence: Owner decided (2026-10-03): R34's core rule is dropped, since every label set shares the one kernel and its cores and a core's timing is no more partitioned than the caches; the confinement check is built in INIT2 by kind (endpoint, volume, network instance, device object, server instance). Written on main at 1d109ac5f (TENETS Confinement and Side channels, init.md The confinement check and R34, SECURITY.md R34 row, GLOSSARY, agents.md); INIT2 cherry-picked it and built the check (d3dc01e79, the confined-* refusal cases on both widths).

### Architect · Owner decision requested

Event: `15e93206429319082a8ca3684fac8129` · 2026-10-02T23:40:14Z

> R34's core rule refuses every confined boot on one hart
> 
> 1. R34 (init.md, the confinement check) refuses a confined manifest that names fewer cores than budget groups. Its reason: time-sharing one core between label sets is a scheduler and timing surface. M1 runs one hart, the manifest has no member for cores, and the steward is a domain of its own. So as written, every confined boot is refused until M2's several harts. Nothing in M1 needs a confined boot; the escape room is M4. What should INIT2 build?
>    - Keep it: no confined boot on one hart (recommended): Recommended. The rule stands as written. With one core, a confined manifest with more than one domain is refused with a cores reason, after every other sharing check has printed its own. A `cores` member and confined boots come with M2's several harts. R34 promises nothing it cannot keep.
>    - Time-share in M1, as a stated residual: The core rule is waived while there is one hart. A confined boot runs, and the shared core is written up as a residual risk on init.md and the tenets' confinement paragraph until M2. Confined boots are testable now, but R34 is weaker than the tenets state.
>    - Add a `cores` member now: The manifest names cores now, and init checks the count against the hart count it learns at boot. On one hart this refuses the same manifests as the first option, plus a new manifest member and a source for the hart count. It is the first option with more surface and no gain until M2.

### Architect · Owner decision requested

Event: `4dfbc19a4b978312aa88dd8bf698ff2a` · 2026-10-03T00:02:16Z

> Confined boots: what they are, and pausing them
> 
> 1. What a confined boot is: the boot manifest may set `confined: true`. That is a whole-machine profile for when label sets must not leak to each other through shared parts. Take Alice's vault label set and Bob's sessions, or two agents in the M4 escape room. Under it, init refuses any layout in which two different label sets share a server process, a volume, an endpoint, a network stack, a device or a CPU core. Any of those could carry state or timing between them. Only the steward and sshd may cross, by audited paths. Without `confined`, servers are shared between users, kept fair by per-domain buckets. That is the normal M1 setup and is unaffected. The core rule cannot be met on M1's one hart, and nothing before M4's escape room needs confinement. Should INIT2 build the confinement check now, or pause it?
>    - Pause it until several harts (recommended): Recommended. INIT2 refuses any manifest that sets `confined`, with the reason 'confined boots are not built yet'. It fails closed, so nobody believes they have confinement. R34 and 'The confinement check' stay planned on init.md, moved from M1 to M4 (self-hosted development), where the escape room needs them. I add a plan node for them that needs M2's several harts. INIT2 gets smaller, and nothing in M1 depends on it.
>    - Build it now, refusing on one hart: INIT2 builds every sharing check as the page states. On one hart, every confined manifest is then refused for cores, after the other checks print their own reasons. The rule is fully tested now, but it is a feature no M1 boot can use.
>    - Build it now, time-sharing the core: INIT2 builds the check without the core rule while there is one hart. A confined boot runs, and the shared core is written up as a residual risk until M2. Confined boots are usable now, but weaker than the tenets promise.

### Architect · Owner decision requested

Event: `b1ffb7d364a025d3741e5c5b5335b5a2` · 2026-10-03T00:04:00Z

> Confined boots share the kernel: drop the core rule?
> 
> 1. Yes, they share a kernel. Every label set, confined or not, runs on the one kernel: its scheduler, its page allocator and its IPC paths. That is by design. The kernel is the trusted base, and budgets and fair scheduling bound what one label set can do to another through it, but its timing is not partitioned. The core rule was the one part of confinement aimed at CPU-level timing (taking turns on a core, the core's own caches). The tenets already admit that the shared second-level cache, memory bandwidth and the kernel itself are not partitioned. So you are right that it goes further than everything around it. Dropping it means a confined boot separates every server, volume, endpoint, network stack and device between label sets, while the kernel and the CPU stay shared. Their timing stays a stated residual risk, as caches already are. The tenets' confinement paragraph changes to match.
>    - Drop the core rule (recommended): Recommended. R34 and the tenets lose 'or core'. The residuals keep 'the scheduler, when two label sets share a core', no longer excepted for confined boots. Confinement covers what software can separate, and nothing it cannot.
>    - Keep the core rule: Confined boots then wait for several harts (M2), and a confined manifest on one hart is refused.
> 2. Without the core rule, the confinement check works on one hart. It is a check on the manifest only, tested on the host and by boot-refusal cases. INIT2's implementer has already designed it. Build it now, or pause it until it is needed (M4's escape room)?
>    - Build it in INIT2 (recommended): Recommended. R34 stays an M1 (separation and containment) rule, as planned. It adds about six attack cases and one check function to INIT2, with no new code paths at boot.
>    - Pause it: INIT2 refuses any manifest that sets `confined`, saying it is not built yet (fail closed). R34 moves to M4 (self-hosted development) with a plan node of its own.
